question: to the Commission Valentina Palmisano (The Left) Subject:

Target M4C1-30 of the Italian national recovery and resilience plan (NRRP) aspires1 to create at least 30 000 new sleeping accommodation units. The Council implementing decision specifies that 30 % of those units must be reserved for students facing socio-economic difficulties and that rents must be at least 15 % below local prices. The same conditions apply to the Student Housing Fund, endowed with EUR 599 million2. According to an investigation by Chora Media3 and Will Media4, in many Italian regions (and particularly in the south), average rents for NRRP-backed accommodation are higher than those for privately rented rooms. What is more, at equal demand, procuring sleeping accommodation units in existing buildings rather than creating new housing capacity limits the increase in supply and ensuing decrease in market prices. These points raise concerns about compliance with the conditions attached to the measures. Can the Commission answer the following: 1.

What data and methodology will it use to check, in accordance with Article 24 of Regulation (EU) 2021/241, that the 15 % reduction relates to the prices actually charged on the local market rather than fees resulting from a ministerial simulation?
Are non-compliant sleeping accommodation units able to be counted towards the M4C1-30 target and eligible to benefit from the fund?
Prior to any assessment, will it ask Italy for data (broken down by structure) on rents, benchmarks, beneficiaries, and units set aside for ‘right to study’ cases, and publish that data?
